# DropSpace v0.3.0-preview.21 — Settings and action usability

<!-- update-summary: Preview.21 makes settings changes field-aware and recoverable, keeps local preferences independent from optional device services, and simplifies Quick Actions with labeled controls, direct checksum copy, and bounded image-size presets. -->

Preview.21 follows the Preview.20 architecture-remediation baseline with a focused usability and reliability pass for the settings and item-action surfaces. It keeps the Windows 10 version 1809 / Build 17763 and later x64 boundary, Dynamic Island product boundary, local-first storage, source-safe export rule, and conditional target-evidence policy.

## Shipped changes

- Settings forms merge only fields edited by that form into the latest persisted snapshot, so a stale page cannot overwrite a newer pause state, update-check timestamp, or unrelated preference. Unchanged startup and device services are not initialized again for a local edit.
- Settings failures identify the affected stage and correlation ID, restore controls on the UI dispatcher, and retry only failed rollback steps. A failed cross-device setup no longer prevents local settings from being saved or retried.
- Primary item actions now use labeled icon-plus-text buttons with descriptions. More actions is visible as a text action, while unavailable network actions remain discoverable with setup guidance.
- SHA-256 runs directly with the default DropSpace export folder, shows a selectable checksum, and offers Copy checksum and Open output folder.
- Image resize and conversion use original, 75%, 50%, and 25% presets with output-dimension feedback; custom pixel fields remain available when needed. Export naming stays collision-safe and never overwrites a source.

## Verification

- Core policy tests build and pass locally: 177 tests, including settings field merging, image preset bounds, and existing regressions.
- C# syntax scan covers `src` and `tests` with zero errors; localization XML/key parity and `git diff --check` pass.
- The Windows CI matrix remains required for WinUI compilation, startup registration, DPI/accessibility, image codec behavior, packaging, installer lifecycle, and manual two-device/network acceptance.

## Conditional target verification

Windows 10 1809/22H2, Windows 11, mixed-DPI and multi-monitor behavior, Explorer/provider/OLE interaction, startup registration, accessibility, physical two-device handoff and clipboard, deployed Worker/browser behavior, and long-run performance remain conditional until directly exercised. Hosted CI and local Linux tests do not substitute for those rows.

The release publishes the five validated Preview assets: `DropSpace-x64.msix`, `DropSpace.exe`, `DropSpaceSetup.exe`, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and `update-manifest.json`. Publication must preserve Preview.20's tag, release, assets, and history.
